name: Aikido Technologies
long_description: We're building GW-scale datacenters in the ocean where there are no limits to the speed and scale of deployment.  Our proprietary offshore platform structure supports a 15MW+ wind turbine, hours of battery storage, backup diesel power generation and 10+ MW of data halls inside their structure, which can be cooled freely by the ocean.

launches.title: Aikido Technologies: GW-scale datacenters at sea
launches.tagline: Aikido deploys clean marine datacenters in weeks, not years
launches.body:
Hi Y’all,

We’re Sam, Bingbin and James and [we’re building AI datacenters out on the ocean](https://youtu.be/k0kcc934lW4?si=068bCBwyDkkNGkM4), powered by the wind and cooled by the sea. Our first unit, A1DC, will hit the water by December and we already have customers lined up to rent the GPUs.

**TLDR:** 

* We’re building datacenters out in the ocean because there is free energy (wind) and free cooling (cold seawater), and no required permits (once you are far enough away from shore);
* Building datacenters out in the ocean is tricky because things break;
* We’ve built [energy infra in the ocean](https://youtu.be/DhHRR_apxmQ?si=UoLwnEfRPLz-nmr5) designed for 25+ years and have developed [our own offshore platform](https://youtu.be/fr8Bh8sTIxM?si=_6eN8AGIvccI2F2I) that is well suited for the integration of AI infrastructure and can be deployed quickly and at scale.

 

**Ask**: 

Can you introduce us to neoclouds, AI labs, inference providers or other compute aggregators who would be interested buying compute on our first 10MW unit? Point them to: [aikidotechnologies.com/reserve](http://aikidotechnologies.com/reserve) 

**Problem:** 

* There are 5+ year wait times for grid connections.
* Conventional energy supply chains are maxed out. Prices for gas turbines have tripled.
* 70% of Americans oppose datacenters in their community. Many states have enacted moratoriums and pauses on datacenter construction and energization, from Texas to New York. 
* New datacenter builds are focused on minimizing friction, not maximizing efficiency nor clean energy. Building GW-scale gas-fired compute close to our cities results can result in a 1deg C localized increase in temps.

**Solution:**

Moving the units out into the ocean solves multiple challenges simultaneously:

* **No Permitting**: Our units don’t impose on the grid nor can be seen by landlubbers;
* **Cheap**: They can be largely powered by the wind (which is stronger and more consistent offshore), and cooled indirectly by the cold seawater.
* **Infinite scale:** No matter where you build in the world, the units are designed and built the same – only the anchoring system differs.
* **Easy Maintenance**: They can be serviced using robotics and existing fleet of offshore vessels and technicians;

**Product:**

Aikido’s product is AO60DC, which we build in farms of 10s-100s. Each platform is the size of a football field and supports:

* 5,000-6,000 GPUs (our first unit will have 78 x GB300 NVL72 racks);
* 15-18MW wind turbine, Hours of battery storage, backup power generation;
* Ultra-low PUE (<1.08);
* Fast and ultra-high bandwidth back to shore via existing subsea fiber;
* Onsite robotic inspection and maintenance (from our friends at Nines);
* On demand human access via vessel or helicopter in 1-4h;

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=125245&key=user_uploads/523370/b1102cd6-d63c-4dd1-a473-9616921aa0be)

**Timeline:**

We started designing our first unit, _A1DC_, back in February; kicked off retrofit of the offshore platform in the US in June, received final permits for the platform in September and will be doing a test fit-up in November. 

We’ve already completed the first stage of the full-scale AO60DC design and will be kicking off the final design, with third-party certification, later this year. We will begin construction next Spring and the unit will hit the water late next year as we look for first customers to rent out the capacity.

**The Team’s Backstory:** 

Bingbin and Sam met back in 2014 at a company that helped build some of the world’s first floating offshore wind, with now 100MW+ in operation. They decided to leave to make offshore wind platforms that were better/cheaper/faster than conventional ones, which were just borrowed from O&G. So they left and joined Otherlab, where they met James, who brings a background in aerospace, designing and building helicopters. They founded Aikido in 2022 with the support of Breakthrough Energy Fellows program (happy to refer folks!) and pivoted from the energy space to the datacenter space in early 2025. 

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=125245&key=user_uploads/523370/ee567cdc-4001-4320-8c62-b5122c3189c2)

The three of us with our first 1:250 scale prototype at a friend’s pool in 2022.
